evidence.source: Shuowen.org, entry for 過; quoting the Shuowen and Duan Yucai’s commentary
evidence.text: The entry gives 過 as “to measure/cross a distance” (度也), formed from 辵 with 咼 as phonetic. Duan says the graph’s sense extended to the 過 in “having faults”; he also reports the distinction of level tone for passing and departing tone for exceeding or fault as a later conventional account.
evidence.title: 說文解字「過」

evidence.source: Taiwan Ministry of Education, Dictionary of Chinese Character Variants
evidence.text: The dictionary cites the Shuowen gloss 度也 and gives examples for senses including passing through, exceeding, excessive degree, visiting, error, and a postverbal experiential/completive particle. Its cited examples include the Zuozhuan-era Mencius passage “三過其門而不入” for passing, and the Analects “由也好勇過我” for exceeding. It supplies classical text references but does not establish when each semantic extension first arose.
evidence.title: [A04167] 過 - 教育部《異體字字典》

evidence.source: Taiwan Ministry of Education, Dictionary of Chinese Character Variants
evidence.text: The entry identifies the regular form as 辵 plus phonetic 咼 and explains that left-side 辶 is the positional form of 辵 in regular script. It records modern Mandarin guò and guō, and cites Guangyun fanqie 古禾切 and 古臥切. This supports distinct level- and departing-tone readings in the dictionary tradition, not a date for their split.
evidence.title: [A04167] 過 - 教育部《異體字字典》

evidence.source: Taiwan Ministry of Education, Dictionary of Chinese Character Variants
evidence.text: The entry calls 过 a long-used俗字 (vulgar/common variant) of 過 and cites Song-Yuan-onward popular-text collections and plays using it. Thus the modern simplified graph is not solely a newly created cursive abbreviation, though later official standardization selected it. The page does not establish the date of the earliest attestation in the cited collection.
evidence.title: [A04167-001] 过 (過) - 教育部《異體字字典》

evidence.text: The received Shuowen entry explicitly analyzes the seal-script form as 辵 plus 咼. This records the Han lexicographer’s analysis; the page’s text does not provide inspectable earlier oracle or bronze forms, so it cannot by itself establish the earliest graphic composition.
evidence.title: 說文解字「過」

evidence.source: 漢字私註, 過 entry; reports attributed analyses by 落合, 白川 and 藤堂
evidence.field: early forms and disputed graphic analysis
evidence.text: This secondary compilation reports an analysis of an oracle-bone form written 𨒵 as 辵 plus 冎, and quotes a claim that a later 口 element produced the current form. It also presents competing interpretations of 咼 as a joint/bone shape or as a ritual element. These are reported scholarly proposals, not independently verified here from the cited oracle-bone plates; the exact earliest form, its use in the cited oracle-bone inscriptions, and whether 咼’s internal shape is historically recoverable remain uncertain.
evidence.title: 過 - 漢字私註

evidence.source: Wiktionary, traditional Chinese entry for 咼, presenting Zhengzhang Shangfang reconstructions
evidence.field: phonetic component pronunciation and proposed role
evidence.text: The entry gives 咼 as Zhengzhang Shangfang Old Chinese *kʰʷroːl and lists 過 among related 咼/冎 phonetic-series graphs, with 過 reconstructed *kloːl and *kloːls. The initial and medial are not identical in these reconstructions, so this series listing is evidence for a proposed historical phonetic relationship, not a perfect sound match. The dossier’s Baxter–Sagart values are a different reconstruction system and should not be mixed with Zhengzhang’s values.
evidence.title: 咼 - 維基詞典，自由的多語言詞典

evidence.text: The entry gives the formation as 辵 plus phonetic 咼 and presents the reading of the Chinese word represented by 過 as Old Chinese *kwaaj in its notation. It lists Mandarin guò and Cantonese gwo3. These are a secondary summary; the Ministry dictionary independently confirms the 辵/咼 analysis and Mandarin readings, while the sound-component relationship is historical rather than a claim that modern readings must match exactly.
evidence.title: 過 - ウィクショナリー日本語版

evidence.source: Wikisource transcription of the 1986 reissued Simplified Character Table
evidence.text: The 1964 joint notice reproduced in the 1986 edition lists 過 → 过 among simplified characters. The table establishes the official mapping, not the earlier cursive pathway; the Taiwan Ministry entry separately records premodern variant use.
evidence.title: 简化字总表（1986年版）

search_audit.query: 說文解字 過 度也 从辵咼聲; 漢語多功能字庫 過 甲骨 金文 字形; 過 字形演變 古文字 字源 辵 咼; Guangyun 過 古禾 古臥 fanqie
search_audit.outcome: Opened Shuowen and Taiwan MOE entries. The MOE page says several paleographic reference tables are unpublished; no primary early-form image was inspected. A non-primary compilation surfaced disputed oracle-bone analyses.

search_audit.query: 咼 Baxter Sagart Old Chinese *kʰʷˤral 過 *kʷˤaj; 咼 中古音 上古音 過 古文字 冎聲; 简化字总表 过 草书 過 简化字 来源; 過 甲骨文 通告 過告 合集 36528
search_audit.outcome: Opened the 咼 entry, official table transcription, and MOE variant entry. Reconstruction evidence available in the inspected page was Zhengzhang Shangfang, not Baxter–Sagart; the Scribd search result was not opened or used.

gaps: No accessible primary oracle-bone or bronze inscription image for 過 was inspected. Claims of an oracle-bone form 𨒵, its use for “notify,” and subsequent addition of 口 remain reported proposals rather than verified findings here.

The origin and original referent of 咼’s internal shape are contested in the inspected secondary account; no primary paleographic evidence resolved whether it depicts bone/joint anatomy or a ritual object.

No dated earliest attestation was established for the sense “pass through” or for later senses such as “exceed,” “fault,” and the experiential particle. Dictionary examples document use but chronology cannot be inferred from their gloss order.

The dossier supplies Baxter–Sagart Old Chinese values for 咼 and 過, but the inspected external material did not independently confirm those exact reconstructions. Zhengzhang reconstructions were inspected and differ in notation and segmental details; do not compare them as though they were one system.

The cursive-origin explanation for simplified 过 was not independently confirmed from inspected historical cursive specimens. The MOE dictionary documents long-standing vernacular variant use, and the official table documents standardization; the precise graphic route remains unresolved.
